items.headline: Stocks ended a rough week with tech and chip stocks leading the drop
items.note: On Friday the S&P 500 fell 1.1% to 7,659.44, the Dow slipped 0.3% to 52,002.41 and the Nasdaq closed at 26,140.03. Chipmakers had their longest losing streak since 2008 on doubts about AI spending. Futures pointed modestly higher early today.

items.headline: Fed raised rates in September; next meeting is Oct 28
items.note: Saxo's recap says the Fed lifted rates to 3.75%-4%, its first increase since 2023, and markets have trimmed odds of another hike this month. Brent crude is near $108 a barrel, which keeps inflation worries alive and matters for tech valuations.

items.headline: A handful of AI-linked stocks drive most of the S&P 500's gains
items.note: ABC (Australia) reports tech is about 44% of the S&P 500 and the top 10 stocks about 39%, up from about 27% at the dot-com peak. Six companies account for 57% of the index's gains since April, so the AI trade matters to the whole market.

items.headline: Anthropic commits 5% of its shares to a public-benefit fund
items.note: Per Anthropic, the fund is subject to stockholder approval and cannot be used for lobbying or political giving.

items.headline: OpenAI confirms it will build a humanoid robot
items.note: Sam Altman told Fortune 'we will definitely do a humanoid'; Engadget reports a demo is targeted for 2027 and OpenAI lists 27 robotics roles, a sign of where ML hiring is heading.

items.headline: US cybersecurity postings fall 26%, but AI security roles surge
items.note: SecurityWeek says postings hit a four-year low of 235,786 in the first nine months of 2026 while AI Security Engineer demand rose 268.3% year over year. AI-specific skills are where demand is.

items.headline: Netflix to lay off about 1,000 staff
items.note: Reported last week; layoffs continue at big tech names even as AI hiring stays strong. Netflix reports earnings Tuesday.

items.headline: Reflection AI open-weights Beam, a 501B-parameter model
items.note: The Apache 2.0 mixture-of-experts model uses 23B active parameters; the company claims about 80% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 with far fewer tokens than GLM-5.2 (a company claim). Free to download and test.

items.headline: Taiwan plans to make AI chip smuggling to China a crime
items.note: The Economic Affairs Minister confirmed unauthorized shipments of AI servers and advanced chips would become an offense under the Foreign Trade Act.

items.headline: Big earnings week: Netflix, Tesla, Meta, IBM
items.note: Per Saxo, Netflix reports Tuesday, Meta, Tesla and IBM Wednesday, and Spotify Thursday. Their AI spending comments could move the sell-off either way.

learn.explain: The S&P 500 is cap-weighted, meaning bigger companies count for more of the index's value. So a few giant stocks can move the whole index. Today's ABC story says the top 10 stocks are about 39% of the S&P 500, and six companies produced 57% of its gains since April. If you own an S&P 500 fund you own all 500 companies, but your results depend heavily on a handful. When those few fall, as chip stocks did last week, the index falls even if most companies are fine.
learn.try: Search for the top 10 holdings of an S&P 500 ETF like VOO and add up their weights.
